mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 3% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 7% for two consecutive months indicates labor market stress, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 7% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% month-over-month signals supply-side stress, which increases input costs and reduces output, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO contracts by more than 2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months indicates broad-based demand weakness, which depresses corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp cut in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by at least 0.75 percentage points within a single month signals an emergency easing, which boosts risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops by >= 0.75% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive after a FEDFUNDS cut of 0.75% or more within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) move in opposite directions for three consecutive months, it signals labor market misalignment, which increases uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE diverge for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE diverge for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the real savings rate (RSAFS) above 8% for four consecutive months signals increased household saving and reduced consumption, which lowers corporate revenue growth and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of strong monetary easing.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 8% for 4 consecutive months and FEDFUNDS not in easing cycle
regime_hint: high savings regime with neutral/contractionary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS > 8% for four months and FEDFUNDS is not in an easing cycle.
